utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- because he was a neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you want to add something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Anto Sliskovic carried out all orders from Mr. Kordic into effect. I took note of that. I have to keep repeating the same question. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that he had some orders that he had to carry out, and in fact he carried out Kordic's orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How much longer are you going to be now, Mr. Naumovski?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Well, I'm sorry, Your Honour, maybe another 10 or 15 minutes at the outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're going to have a five-minute break. We'll then hear you for ten minutes and hope we can finish the evidence today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ten minutes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have just collected my thoughts, and I may just make it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, you said that Mr. Sliskovic carried out all Mr. Kordic's orders, but then later on you elaborated and said that all lower-level commanders were accountable to Anto Sliskovic and then he, in turn, to Mr. Kordic; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I think it can be said. Anto Sliskovic's employees obviously were accountable to him, and he again to Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how do you know that, when his commander at the time was Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: What do you mean "Blaskic"? Dario Kordic was God Almighty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, please, do you know a single example of lower commanders reporting to Anto Sliskovic and he to Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: What kind of example do you want? Could a single Muslim see anything of the sort?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So apart from your conclusions, you do not know of a single example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, I think we've had this point several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the Jokers were also based in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the Jokers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: A punitive unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I must tell you, Mr. J, that they were not headquartered in Busovaca, but there were some of them in Busovaca, sir. Are we talking about their headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's less important in my view, but they were in Busovaca as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, if you say so. When you were in Kaonik, you mentioned several examples about what happened to you, so I should like to ask you, very briefly, when you were interrogated by certain people, including Zarko Petrovic and Zeljko Katava, you said that certain questions were put to you, but I'm not sure I heard what kind of questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: All kinds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Military questions as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: One could call them that. They did ask at one point where the radio was, radio transmitter was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Yesterday you also said that one day, military policemen had beaten one of the soldiers and that they did so on purpose so that the Muslims would see them doing it. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was on the 8th of February, 1993, in the morning, in prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that those people were released the next day; nothing happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to the people who stayed on in prison, and there were some who stayed on, they were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honour, I should like to tender a document connected to this event that we are talking about, and that is the killing of these two Muslims that the witness referred to, Jasmin Sehovic and Nermin Elezovic. A copy for the witness, please. The Croatian version is at the back.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D38/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) While Mr. J is waiting to examine his copy, let me, in order to gain time, tell you briefly what this is. It is a criminal complaint submitted by the 4th military police battalion against three soldiers, Croats, under suspicion that they had killed these two Muslims that the witness referred to. The second document is a request for an investigation to be carried out whereby the judge of the basic military court in Travnik prescribes an investigation into the event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, will you look at those documents, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Please give the witness the Croatian copy so he can look at them. The criminal report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the factual description at the bottom, you will find that there are grounds to believe that they committed -- so and so, and the data about the two individuals are mentioned. Are they the people you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) We don't need to tire Their Honours further with this exhibit. You may collect it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go on, Mr. J. Tell us, please, when you were released, or exchanged, I don't remember you telling us, did you see a doctor in Zenica, to be examined?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did go to see a doctor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any medical reports about your injuries? Because you said that you were full of injuries.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think I do, but not on me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't show them to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No one asked me to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not even regarding your jaw fracture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Briefly about two events: When you referred to the event in the village of Strane that your brother or this other group of people told you about, people who were taken there, as you were not there, did they tell you there was no shooting there, in the village of Strane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that was the first time, and I think there was no shooting, as far as I can recollect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As for the second event, in the village of Merdani, you said that if they do not surrender, and the implication is the inhabitants, that all these people would be slaughtered; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did the villagers surrender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone killed? Was this threat carried out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that punishment of perpetrators was not even prescribed in HVO documents. Do you still abide by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Exactly. Maybe it was written down somewhere, but nothing came of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a conversation with Mr. Glavocevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were you with at that meeting, and in what capacity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the time, we were still the Patriotic League. Others called us differently. And two of us, myself and Ekmiscic, went to see Florijan Glavocevic and put ourselves at his disposal to see if there was anything we could do to help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That he would see about it with Mr. Dario.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That he would consult him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. However, we never got any reply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Just one more question, one but last. When you said that Mr. Sliskovic offered that you go in the direction of Lugovi to help the front line, in what capacity did you go to see Mr. Sliskovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: We didn't go to see him. He came to see us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you mean, "us"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Us in the Patriotic League, in the fire brigade centre. He came one night, and we spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I am looking through my papers very quickly. If I take more time, I will find at least another ten questions to put, but I will end there. Thank you for your patience. I have no further questions. And I thank you, too, Mr. J.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. J. My name is Mikulicic. I am the Defence counsel for Mr. Mario Cerkez, and I am going to ask you a few questions, and I would like to ask you to answer them. Tell us, please, Mr. J, did you serve in the former JNA, the former army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you assigned any rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was a private first class.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, would you tell us, after you completed your military service, were you in the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that was quite normal in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your duties as a reservist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I was a (indiscernible).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any weapons in that capacity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. We were only issued weapons if there was any kind of training or anything like that, and then we would return it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us, please, what type of weapons were issued, what kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, at that time there were semi-automatic rifles. There were also automatic rifles as well. There were M52s and old types of machine guns. But for the most part it was these two types of rifles that were predominant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, would you tell us, please, whether you are a religious man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I am a believer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you practice your religion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that's difficult to say, and it's my own private affair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the imam from Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, during the time you were in Kaonik, did the imam from Busovaca go to Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, after the independence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you were a member of the Territorial Defence, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, we all were, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you issued any weapons in that capacity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that on the 25th of January, 1993, the alarm was sounded in Busovaca, and that immediately after that, shooting started. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the alarm sounded by means of a siren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, a fire brigade siren. Fire alarm siren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "fire alarm siren," does that mean that the siren was in the fire brigade building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Not far away from where we were, across the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in the fire brigade building, there was the headquarters of the Patriotic League for Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It was located there at one time, once upon a time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, Mr. J, that some soldiers attacked your house and that it was riddled with bullets, and that at one point you retaliated. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I responded by opening fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What weapon did you use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had a Scorpion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you said that you were issued no weapons. Where did you get that Scorpion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I bought it myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you buy that type of weapon in shops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, in the former Yugoslavia, you couldn't buy anything normally, particularly not weapons in a shop. You would have to have a special permit. But, of course, in those days and the days that followed, there were no rules, and people bought what they found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, you were taken to Kaonik, and you said that there were a lot of men there. You said that there were people of different ages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of those men who were with you there in Kaonik who were outside military age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think there were two or three very young boys who were under the age of 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think, or do you know for certain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know for certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that would be difficult now, but I do know that there was a young man from Skradno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, when you came to Kaonik, did you see a board of any kind, or a plaque on the building, or the neighbouring building, where you were located later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything of that kind, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see any kind of plaque or board indicating the type of building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. J, that you told us that on the first day when you were brought to Kaonik -- that is to say, on the 25th of January, 1993 -- you were addressed by Zlatko Aleksovski as the warden, commander of that facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, if I were to tell you that in the indictment of this Court against Mr. Aleksovski, the Prosecutor stated that he took over the Kaonik facility on the 29th of January, what would your comments to that be? Do you allow for the possibility of being wrong with the dates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Absolutely no theory that that could have happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, you said that when you came to Kaonik, all your personal possessions were taken away from you, your valuables?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, almost everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they or were they not confiscated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, things were taken away. Bags full of money were taken away. Anybody who did not succeed in hiding their valuables, they were taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you succeed in hiding anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us, Mr. J, that some 15 people were taken out from the building, tied, 13 were tied, and they were then taken to be used in what we call a human shield at the village of Strane, but that you were not amongst those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I then conclude correctly that what happened at the village of Strane you only know from what those people told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know it from what my brother told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the village of Strane, were there any units of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, as far as I know, there were none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your brother tell you how far the people we're talking about were positioned with respect to the village of Strane, in relation to the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I personally don't remember those details, but as the main road passes below the village, then they were very near the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us the place they were located at? Did your brother tell you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't think -- no, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with respect to the village of Merdani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: The village of Merdani? Well, there it was somewhat different. They were kept there the whole day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, Mr. J, is whether perhaps you can tell us the position in relation to the village of Merdani, because you said that they were on the railway bridge, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they were positioned there, but up to the village of Merdani, there is still two kilometres to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Mr. J, whether any of these individuals were wounded or injured.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, let us now touch upon the events when you returned from Putis. A moment ago, mention was made of that, and you said that you were guarded by some young men from the HVO who were from Vitez, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is the following: How do you know that those young men were from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: They guarded us throughout the night, and based on our conversations with them, and they were very, very good towards us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you spent the entire night with those soldiers, do you know which unit they were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, do you know somebody called Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I've heard the name, but -- well, I've heard the name, yes, but I can't tell you anything definite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just tell us, do you know whether he was the commander of any unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, everything I know, I know from what people have said: that he was the commander and had a unit of his own. I know something about that, but not in concrete terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't really know, because it was another municipality, so that I didn't know those people. I didn't know Darko, either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they the Vitezovi, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that that was what their name was; something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, you said that you noticed while you were in Kaonik that there were lists of people made up for work duty, for digging. Do you know where these lists came from? Who compiled those lists? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, how could I know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't, then? Thank you. Tell us, please, Mr. J, whether the guards in Kaonik were also in military uniform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they wore camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you manage to see what unit they belonged to? What kind of soldiers were they? What type?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, some of them had an HVO patch, as far as I recall, but I don't know anything else, any other characteristic feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they carry weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the prison itself, they didn't have any weapons. When they came to our cells, they did not have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you managed to save some of your valuables; do you mean the two rings and the money that you gave to Hosovac later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, precisely that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that those objects were returned to you after this Hosovac was arrested by the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. The two rings were returned to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers, Mr. J.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The Defence rests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Scott, there is really very little time indeed. Is there anything by way of re-examination of any importance?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you just give me one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, during the pause, at an appropriate time I would like to address the Court relative to expert witness Alcock, who is in our view -- according to the Prosecution is to be called next week, but we don't have his full statement. So if there is a problem, then I would like to raise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Very good, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could, very briefly, I will move quickly. Re-examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness J, in reference, I'm not going to ask the usher to show them to you, but you were shown several exhibits: 37/1, 38/1, and 39/1. Had you seen any of those documents prior to the time that they were showed to you in court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any information about their authenticity or existence prior to the time they were shown to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I forget, I would just ask for the record at this time that in reference to 39/1, on the second page of that document, there is fairly long list of attachments. Under the rule of completeness, the Prosecution would ask that all those attachments be provided to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. J, in terms of the questions you were asked about the defensive positions, in what Mr. Naumovski called the defensive positions in Busovaca on the 25th of January -- I think you can answer this "Yes" or "No" -- was there any organised defence or military resistance to the HVO attack on Busovaca on the 25th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consider those men to be assembled for the purposes of filling -- or taking position in a military sense?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, no, of course not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, concerning this witness -- concerning the speech that Mr. Kordic gave, you've said that you know this person, but you do not want to name him in court, presumably out of concern for his privacy or security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, in case there's some further follow-up, are you prepared to provide that name to the Prosecution so that we can pursue this matter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Finally, Witness J, you testified in direct examination that based on the best of your memory, the population of Busovaca in 1992/1993 was approximately some 8.000. If I represent to you, please, as an officer of the Court, that the 1991 census would show that the Busovaca population was approximately 3.900 people, would you have any reason to disagree with that? The town of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, all right, in the town of Busovaca itself, probably the population did number that much, but the municipality had 16.000 inhabitants, as far as I remember. Perhaps I meant the broader area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just two pop questions following on that, Your Honour, and I'll be concluded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In short, is it fair to say, Witness J, Busovaca was a small town, and the people who lived there and had lived there for many years tended to know a lot, if not everything, that happened in town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would be particularly true of anyone who might be described as having a high profile position, such as a mayor or a political leader? People knew a lot about those things, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness J, thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give your evidence. I'm sorry you've been detained here as long as you have, but you are now released and free to go home. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Tomorrow afternoon, I think I'm right on saying, on this occasion, it will be half past 2.00.
